nodes.label: LoopGuard
nodes.rationale: Local circuit breaker for AI coding agents; capabilities are not advertised until platform integration tests pass, and unsupported agent/platform combinations fail closed so the local breaker stays useful without hosted services.

nodes.label: Protected Path Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The core policy decision is synchronous and durable before acknowledgement; a crash after persistence is replayed without double-applying detector state or completed handler work.

nodes.label: Local Control Plane
nodes.rationale: Framed owner-authenticated daemon with encrypted SQLite log; Windows named-pipe transport stays capability-gated until a real current-user named-pipe backend passes native tests.

nodes.label: Auto-Heal
nodes.rationale: Repairs are bounded to isolated reproduction, verification, and a draft PR; Auto-Heal cannot merge or deploy.

nodes.label: Production NO-GO Status
nodes.rationale: Public beta/GA are blocked until live staging load, encrypted restore, regional failover/failback, signed release, real identity/payment providers, legal terms, and named human sign-offs complete; the project chooses stated honesty over premature launch.

nodes.label: awaiting_owner_legal_choice Distribution Gate
nodes.rationale: No license file exists, so no redistribution or production-use rights may be inferred until the owner makes an explicit legal choice.

nodes.label: LoopGuard Changelog
nodes.rationale: Packages follow Semantic Versioning while API, protocol, event, workflow, and database contracts carry explicit independent versions.

nodes.label: cloud-app Expo Prototype Deprecation
nodes.rationale: The Expo prototype remains available for one release for migration comparison and is scheduled for removal no earlier than 0.3.0; users move to apps/web and apps/ios.

nodes.label: Community Code of Conduct
nodes.rationale: Enforcement decisions weigh context, impact, pattern, and repair rather than popularity; conduct reports go privately to the repository owner.

nodes.label: Change Workflow
nodes.rationale: Add a failing test first, implement the smallest complete change, regenerate generated indexes when sources change, and report skipped gates explicitly — a skip is not a pass.

nodes.label: Private Vulnerability Reporting
nodes.rationale: Acknowledge receipt within two business days and give an initial disposition within five; these are response targets, not a promised fix date.

nodes.label: Pull Request Template
nodes.rationale: Requires exact command evidence, safety/operations checkboxes, and rollout/rollback description; a skipped gate is not a pass.

nodes.label: Bug Report Template
nodes.rationale: Requires a privacy confirmation and redacted doctor output so no prompts, source, secrets, or production identifiers leak into public issues.

nodes.label: Feature Request Template
nodes.rationale: Asks for the developer problem, current workaround cost, and desired outcome without prescribing an implementation.

nodes.label: Web Verification Job
nodes.rationale: Runs the built web container read-only with tmpfs and checks /health for the exact build SHA before any OCI artifact is recorded.

nodes.label: Publish Signed Web Image Job
nodes.rationale: Runs only on manual dispatch with the client-web-production environment; signs the immutable image digest with cosign.

nodes.label: control-foundation CI Workflow
nodes.rationale: Runs the loopguard package suite warning-strict on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows and verifies the generated CLI reference has not drifted.

nodes.label: deploy Workflow
nodes.rationale: Deployment accepts only immutable private ECR digests cosign-verified against the tagged release workflow identity, keeping unsigned or foreign images out of the cluster; migration is rehearsed before any canary.

nodes.label: Isolated API Canary Deployment
nodes.rationale: The canary is probed via port-forward without public traffic before signed digests are promoted atomically; any failure rolls back to the captured Helm revision and uploads evidence.

nodes.label: public-docs Workflow
nodes.rationale: Regenerates the OpenAPI contract, CLI reference, and docs indexes, then rejects any generated-reference drift with git diff --exit-code so published references stay in lockstep with source.

nodes.label: Sign and Verify Job
nodes.rationale: Every artifact gets a digest-bound SBOM/SLSA predicate and keyless cosign attestation, and the assembled manifest is verified before upload.

nodes.label: Release Publish Job
nodes.rationale: Reverifies the release manifest before any external write and only runs on manual dispatch with production-release environment approval for a version tag.

nodes.label: security Workflow
nodes.rationale: Dependency review is non-blocking only because private repos without Advanced Security reject the API; the Python/JavaScript audits, pinned Gitleaks scan, and Trivy container scan remain blocking.

nodes.label: LoopGuard iOS App Target
nodes.rationale: Swift 6 with complete strict concurrency and warnings-as-errors; OIDC endpoints are placeholder .invalid hosts in build settings.

nodes.label: LoopGuard Cloud Expo Prototype
nodes.rationale: Retained one release as a local/demo migration fallback only; unauthenticated with open CORS and in-memory server state, so it must never be exposed to the public internet.

nodes.label: Mission Control Screen
nodes.rationale: On a flagged loop it shows a decision card with four genuine actions — Approve fix, Continue once, Allow tool, Terminate — plus free-text correction.

nodes.label: Legacy Demo Server (loopguard serve)
nodes.rationale: Defaults to loopback; a LAN demo requires an explicit temporary --host 0.0.0.0 flag on a trusted network because this compatibility path has no auth.

nodes.label: LoopGuard Cloud Design System
nodes.rationale: The interface is dark because it is a monitoring surface, not for decorative glow; green/amber/red are semantic statuses only and must pair with an icon or text label.

nodes.label: OKLCH Design Tokens
nodes.rationale: tokens.css is the portable OKLCH source and src/theme.ts holds converted opaque sRGB values; raw colour values may appear only in the token module.

nodes.label: Control API Endpoint Contract
nodes.rationale: All /v1 paths require a verified tenant principal and return the RFC 9457 problem union; cross-tenant detail IDs return the same 404 as absent IDs so tenancy cannot be probed.

nodes.label: Signed Idempotent Actions
nodes.rationale: Action HTTP acceptance is never an execution receipt; clients reconcile by action ID instead of retrying blindly, and challenges are one-use.

nodes.label: One-Use Stream Tickets
nodes.rationale: Browser WebSocket upgrades carry only a 30-second one-use ticket (with CSRF for cookies) while native upgrades carry a bearer header.

nodes.label: Cursor Domain Separation
nodes.rationale: Relay upload cursors (local_log_seq), global cloud ingestion (cloud_ingest_seq), and stream replay (session_seq) are deliberately non-interchangeable to prevent cross-domain replay confusion.

nodes.label: Plain-English Product Guide
nodes.rationale: Positions LoopGuard as a seat belt and flight recorder for coding agents: stop obvious loops, record safely, require proof before risky changes.

nodes.label: Four Connected Product Layers
nodes.rationale: Local Python guard, managed Codex/Claude adapters, multi-tenant control API with signed actions, and Auto-Heal; local guarding stays useful even if the hosted service is unavailable.

nodes.label: Auto-Heal Repair Workflow
nodes.rationale: Eight bounded steps from allowlisted fetch to draft PR; if evidence is incomplete the result stays inconclusive, and if any budget, quota, policy, sandbox, or verification gate fails no PR is published.

nodes.label: Offline Quickstart
nodes.rationale: Proves the real protected path with three synthetic hook-shaped events and no API key, cloud account, Docker, telemetry, or permanent hooks; it never reads provider-key environment variables.

nodes.label: Respond to a Loop Stop Guide
nodes.norm_label: respond to a loop stop guide

nodes.label: Loop Detection Categories
nodes.rationale: Exact repeated tool call, semantically equivalent work, ping-pong between two states, repeated failure without new evidence, or a configured time/turn/cost budget.

nodes.label: Narrowest Safe Response Principle
nodes.rationale: A stop is a safety decision, not proof the agent is wrong; choose the narrowest action (interrupt, redirect, request evidence, approve bounded action, or start repair) and fix false stops with a synthetic regression test rather than globally disabling protection.

nodes.label: Demo v1 to Control v1 Migration Guide
nodes.norm_label: demo v1 to control v1 migration guide

nodes.label: Backup-First Encrypted Local Migration
nodes.rationale: Snapshot SQLite including committed WAL, encrypt with a key held in the platform credential service, verify the backup by decrypting in memory, then apply forward-only migrations so a failed migration is always restorable. Lost in-memory demo data is never invented from screenshots or logs, and downgrades by editing PRAGMA user_version are forbidden.

nodes.label: Platform Credential Service (Keychain/DPAPI/libsecret)
nodes.rationale: OS credential services protect the encryption key; the encrypted-file fallback prints an explicit warning and is not the preferred production configuration.

nodes.label: Stripe Webhook HMAC Verification
nodes.rationale: HMAC over the exact raw body with at most five minutes of clock skew, server-side tenant binding, and evt_ deduplication so forged, stale, malformed, unbound, or replayed webhooks fail closed. Provider creation time orders entitlement changes so an older event cannot roll back newer state.

nodes.label: Entitlement State Machine (active/grace/blocked/deleted)
nodes.rationale: Payment failure or expired grace blocks only new hosted expensive work; local guarding, read, export, delete, and security paths are always available so billing state can never destroy evidence or interrupt local protection.

nodes.label: Immutable Versioned Price Catalog
nodes.rationale: Each usage entry pins its catalog version so a mid-period price change produces separate invoice lines at old and new prices; USD lines use decimal arithmetic rounding half-up to cents, and binary floating point is forbidden.

nodes.label: Invoice Reconciliation Against Usage Ledger
nodes.rationale: Invoices are rebuilt from the immutable usage ledger; a difference other than $0.00 blocks finalization, and credits/refunds/corrections are new signed, audited adjustment records rather than edits to existing lines.

nodes.label: Tenant-Scoped Backpressure
nodes.rationale: LoopGuard accepts work only when it can preserve it and never returns success for silently dropped work; limits are tenant-scoped so a noisy tenant cannot affect another tenant, and 429 LGAPI-OVERLOADED responses include Retry-After plus bounded deterministic jitter that spreads clients without making retries unpredictable.

nodes.label: Default Production Limit Envelope
nodes.rationale: All limits are explicit LOOPGUARD_API_* settings; the initial defaults are conservative bootstrap values, not a capacity claim, and production changes require a load result, dashboard review, and a rollback value.

nodes.label: k6 Ingest and Stream Load Gates
nodes.rationale: The checked-in k6 scenarios are the release gate; no synthetic laptop result is represented as production capacity, and the authoritative result must be attached to each staging release with at least 30% measured headroom.
nodes.norm_label: k6 ingest and stream load gates

nodes.label: Keyless Cosign Web Image Signing
nodes.rationale: The web release identity is its immutable digest, published and signed with keyless Cosign only under GitHub environment protection; rollback selects a previously verified digest, never a mutable tag, and no deployment runs from the release job.

nodes.label: TestFlight-Only iOS Release
nodes.rationale: CI archives with a unique build number and uploads to TestFlight only, never submitting for App Review; a human release operator reviews TestFlight results and starts App Review separately, and TestFlight builds are immutable and expired rather than overwritten.

nodes.label: Bounded Metric Cardinality and Log Redaction
nodes.rationale: Dashboard variables never use tenant/user/resource IDs as metric dimensions; the telemetry library rejects forbidden attribute names and unbounded labels in tests, and collector processors drop payload, prompt, source code, tool args/output, token, secret, credential, authorization, and private-key keys before export so observability cannot leak tenant content.
nodes.norm_label: bounded metric cardinality and log redaction

nodes.label: Private Multi-AZ EKS Reference Topology
nodes.rationale: Terraform manages VPC, subnets, private EKS endpoint, dedicated system and repair node groups, RDS, S3/KMS, ECR, ACM, and Route 53, but receives secret ARNs and never secret values; the Helm chart references only Kubernetes Secrets, and no implicit cluster-creator admin back door exists.

nodes.label: Signed-Digest Deploy Workflow
nodes.rationale: Accepts only repository@sha256 digest inputs verified with Cosign against the release workflow identity, exchanges GitHub OIDC for a short-lived AWS role, rehearses migrations on an isolated database, canaries through a private port-forward, and rolls back to the captured Helm revision on failure; tags, latest, public registries, and long-lived AWS keys are rejected, and production approval is a required human gate.

nodes.label: Two-Phase Terraform/Helm Bootstrap
nodes.rationale: The first deployment is deliberately two-phase because an ALB hostname does not exist before the chart creates its ingress; Terraform is applied with an empty hostname, the chart is installed, then Terraform is reapplied with the observed ALB hostname.

nodes.label: Warm DR Region and Operator-Authorized Promotion
nodes.rationale: Multi-AZ is not regional failover; DR promotion is operator-authorized and requires fencing the former writer, integrity and idempotency validation before any Route 53 change, and a preserved failback path. Rehearsal wrappers must never point at production.
nodes.norm_label: warm dr region and operator-authorized promotion

nodes.label: Repair Pod Isolation (gVisor)
nodes.rationale: Repair pods run under a gVisor RuntimeClass on isolated nodes with no host filesystem, container socket, cloud role, service-account token, or metadata endpoint, so a malicious repair candidate cannot reach the host or cloud account.

nodes.label: RPO 5 min / RTO 60 min Targets
nodes.rationale: These are objectives, not claims; a release may advertise them only after the quarterly isolated restore and regional exercise record timestamps that meet both budgets.

nodes.label: Encrypted age Recovery Bundle
nodes.rationale: backup.sh uses pg_dump custom format, captures integrity invariants, validates the object manifest, hashes every component, packages only four allowlisted files, encrypts with a KMS-controlled age recipient before publishing, and writes owner-only permissions; restore.sh refuses a target URL equal to the source and rejects traversal, links, and checksum mismatches before pg_restore.

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Restore Integrity Verification
nodes.rationale: A restore is not usable until ingest sequences, per-session replay positions, artifact SHA-256 hashes, and persisted action resolutions match the encrypted backup; application traffic stays disabled until schema health, tenant RLS, OIDC, Temporal visibility, object reads, stream replay, and a signed action canary all pass.

nodes.label: Expand/Backfill/Read-Switch/Contract Migration Sequencing
nodes.rationale: Every destructive schema change is split across releases so old and new binaries coexist; contract happens only after old binaries are drained and rollback has expired, and any lock over 30 seconds or observed old/new incompatibility blocks release.

nodes.label: SEV-0 to SEV-3 Severity Classification
nodes.rationale: A cross-tenant result, accepted-and-lost event/action, corrupted restore, or signature bypass is always an incident even when aggregate SLOs look healthy; anyone may declare an incident.

nodes.label: Incident Roles and Human Authority
nodes.rationale: No person both requests and approves break glass; database promotion, DNS failover, user-affecting credential rotation, destructive cleanup, and customer notification require a named human authority, and a privacy/legal owner (never an implementation agent) decides notification.

nodes.label: Stabilize/Contain/Investigate/Eradicate/Recover Loop
nodes.rationale: Containment disables the narrowest affected capability while keeping local guarding and export/deletion available; recovery never bypasses signature or tenant controls, and cause is not attributed before evidence supports it.

nodes.label: Append-Only Tenant-Scoped Usage Ledger
nodes.rationale: Every entry carries a tenant-bound idempotent usage_id, category, finite positive units, provider cost where applicable, and the exact price-catalog version active when the usage occurred; replaying an identical ID is a no-op while reuse with different semantics fails and alerts. Local guarding is never metered.

nodes.label: Reserve/Commit/Release Quota Transaction
nodes.rationale: Expensive hosted work atomically reserves estimated units before side effects, commits exact usage after durable completion, and releases on cancellation/timeout/failure so a rejected job is never accepted or silently dropped; repair admission checks billing grace before workflow capacity.

nodes.label: Metered Unit Categories
nodes.rationale: Seven explicit categories (storage byte-hours, retained events, compute seconds, judge USD, critic USD, browser minutes, repair worker seconds); provider cost and LoopGuard charge are separate fields, and avoided-cost estimates are explanatory, never billed.

nodes.label: NO-GO Decision for Beta/GA
nodes.rationale: Code completion is not production approval: live-environment exercises, durable hosted adapters, provider activation, legal terms, and human sign-offs remain blocking, and empty evidence is a failure. No implementation agent may self-sign, apply production infrastructure, promote a database, switch DNS, activate billing, publish, or notify customers.

nodes.label: Gate-by-Gate Evidence Ledger
nodes.rationale: Each gate names its owner, evidence artifacts, last exercise, and evidence expiry; automated per-build tests do not stand in for named staging or human exercises, and a failed target creates a blocking defect that is not waived in a meeting.

nodes.label: Release Manifest (artifacts/release/manifest.json)
nodes.rationale: Binds every output (wheel, npm tarball, OCI images, iOS archive) to the exact build commit, SHA-256, SPDX/CycloneDX SBOM, SLSA/in-toto provenance, and Sigstore bundle; images use immutable digests, never mutable tags, and paths may not escape the release directory.

nodes.label: CI Trust Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Actions are pinned to immutable commit SHAs, permissions start read-only, untrusted PR code never runs in pull_request_target or receives secrets, and outputs move between jobs only through checksummed artifacts so a compromised PR cannot reach signing credentials.

nodes.label: verify_release.sh Cosign Verification
nodes.rationale: Checks every checksum and evidence binding, then runs cosign verify-blob/verify with the manifest's exact GitHub workflow identity and OIDC issuer; any missing tool, mismatched commit, wrong digest, symlink, traversal, or failed signature fails the entire release and lists all defects.

nodes.label: SLO Catalog
nodes.rationale: Eight capability SLOs (local durability 99.99%, cloud ingest 99.95%, relay latency, action resolution 99.9%, stream replay 99.99%, verification 99%, repair workflow 99%, API availability 99.95%) measured from server/worker metrics plus synthetic probes, never client-only analytics; explicit overload rejections are reported separately from availability.

nodes.label: Burn-Rate Alerting Policy
nodes.rationale: Multi-window burn rates (5-minute 14.4x with 1-hour 6x pages immediately; 30-minute 6x with 6-hour 3x pages during coverage); alerts carry correlation IDs, digest, runbook, and dashboard but never prompts, source, credentials, or payment data.

nodes.label: Correlation IDs and Bounded Sampling
nodes.rationale: Request/event/session/action/workflow IDs propagate on traces and logs for investigation but are never metric labels; errors are sampled at 100% while SLI counters remain unsampled, and local telemetry is opt-in and disabled by default.

nodes.label: Consent-Bound Support Access
nodes.rationale: Tenant administrators grant time-bounded metadata_health or diagnostic_bundle scopes with reason, ticket, and expiry; diagnostic access recomputes the redacted bundle and fails closed on any difference from the approved preview hash. There is no silent impersonation and no support role can approve or execute a remote action.

nodes.label: Dual-Approval Break Glass
nodes.rationale: Limited to metadata health, expires within one hour, requires two different support approvers, alerts the tenant on grant, is fully audited, and never unlocks diagnostics or remote actions; used only when waiting for ordinary consent would materially increase harm.

nodes.label: Enterprise Identity (OIDC/SAML/SCIM)
nodes.rationale: SCIM bearer secrets are shown once and stored as salted scrypt hashes with a deployment pepper; OIDC/SAML setup requires a verified DNS TXT challenge, an email domain alone never authorizes a role, deprovisioning is soft and preserves audit, and hosted startup rejects the checked-in deterministic test adapters.

nodes.label: Reconcile Ambiguous Actions by ID
nodes.rationale: Never fix an ambiguous result by creating another action; reconcile the existing action ID against the authoritative host outcome and immutable audit chain, and rotate signing material only under the security-owner procedure with a documented key overlap.

nodes.label: Relay Outage Safety Invariants
nodes.rationale: Local guarding continues offline; never return success before durable cloud acceptance; never discard or reorder a local outbox record to reduce queue depth; ambiguous remote actions are reconciled by ID, not blindly retried.

nodes.label: Runbook: Disable Auto-Heal Safely
nodes.rationale: Stop new repair admission and draft-PR publication without stopping local protection; never attach a host filesystem, container socket, service-account token, or cloud role to inspect a candidate, and restore in stages ending with one canary draft PR in an authorized test repository.

nodes.label: Per-Category Retention Policy
nodes.rationale: Defaults come from loopguard_api.retention.DEFAULT_RETENTION_DAYS (events 30 days hosted, verification 90, actions/audit 365, tombstones 2,555); retention changes are versioned and audited and never shorten a legal minimum without privacy/legal approval, and legal hold is explicit per record without granting support access.

nodes.label: HMAC Deletion Tombstone
nodes.rationale: Deletion checkpoints PostgreSQL, object storage/replicas, Temporal search attributes, notification tokens, and derived metrics separately, is idempotent, and resumes without repeating completed destructive stages; completion writes only an HMAC tenant reference, workflow ID, completion time, and stage count.

nodes.label: Tenant-Scoped Export Workflow
nodes.rationale: Export is deterministic-manifested and excludes access/refresh tokens, private keys, credentials, authorization headers, and presigned URLs; the caller encrypts the bundle, and export URLs are short-lived and audience-bound.

nodes.label: Web Console
nodes.rationale: The broad operational workbench for runs, changes, verification, hosts, policies, cost, devices, and immutable audit; requires a registered user-verified WebAuthn assertion for action confirmation and is Axe-checked to WCAG 2.0/2.1 A/AA plus 2.2 AA on every core route.

nodes.label: Native SwiftUI iOS App
nodes.rationale: The focused safety client for attention, proof-first run inspection, device security, notifications, and signed action review; signs with its paired device key and requires device-owner authentication for server-designated high-risk actions.

nodes.label: Capability-Gated Navigation (repair.ready)
nodes.rationale: Neither client invents capability: navigation and controls come from authenticated server state, Repairs stays completely absent until the server reports a fresh available repair.ready capability, and unknown, stale, unavailable, or revoked inputs fail closed.

nodes.label: Signed Action Review Contract
nodes.rationale: Review shows the exact target, effect, risk, parameter hash, expected state, and expiry; HTTP acceptance is only queued work, execution renders only with a daemon-derived receipt, and expiry, changed content, host loss, revocation, or acknowledgement ambiguity never triggers an automatic re-sign or resubmit.

nodes.label: Draft-Only Repair Publication
nodes.rationale: Publication is a high-risk signed action bound to the repair's exact state version and hash; it can only create a draft pull request — LoopGuard cannot merge or deploy it — and an ambiguous response is reconciled by action ID rather than publishing again.

nodes.label: Deprecated cloud-app Compatibility Fallback
nodes.rationale: cloud-app remains available for one release as an explicit fallback with no silent redirect; no new production architecture, security, or workflow behavior may be added to it, and it is removed only in a later, separately announced release.

nodes.label: Semantic Colour Tokens
nodes.rationale: Only token files contain raw colour values; components consume semantic names (paper/rule/ink/accent/success/warning/danger), every semantic colour is paired with text and an icon, and the accent stays under roughly 3% of a viewport.

nodes.label: Status Grammar
nodes.rationale: Five status families (success, attention, blocking, active/transport, neutral) each pair label, symbol family, and colour; status copy names the observed condition before offering a remedy, and 'Something went wrong' is banned.

nodes.label: Truth Rule
nodes.rationale: Never invent cost savings, success rates, urgency, health, or completion; unknown, stale, skipped, pre-existing, and inconclusive are real states with their own language, and the product reports state rather than performing urgency through decoration.

nodes.label: Liquid Glass Boundary
nodes.rationale: On iOS 26 native Liquid Glass is limited to tab/navigation and transient controls while evidence, timelines, and approval content stay on standard surfaces; glass remains prohibited in the Expo prototype and glassmorphism is prohibited entirely on web.

nodes.label: Accessibility Release Contract (WCAG 2.2 AA)
nodes.rationale: Web targets WCAG 2.2 AA with 4.5:1 body contrast; iOS supports VoiceOver, Voice Control, Differentiate Without Color, Increase Contrast, Reduce Motion, Bold Text, and the largest accessibility Dynamic Type size; keyboard/VoiceOver order follows visual and risk order with raw logs never preceding current state, proof, or action.

nodes.label: Local Guarding Independence from Billing
nodes.rationale: LoopGuard's local circuit breaker is independent from hosted billing: a hosted payment failure, quota exhaustion, or provider outage never disables local guarding, data export/deletion, security actions, or read-only access.

nodes.label: Transparent Billing Dimensions
nodes.rationale: If hosted billing is activated the immutable catalog can price only seven explicit units (storage byte-hour, retained event, compute second, judge USD, critic USD, browser minute, repair worker second); upstream provider cost and customer charge are separate fields, and avoided-cost estimates are never billable.

nodes.label: LoopGuard CLI Reference
nodes.rationale: Generated from the installed Typer command tree via python -m loopguard.cli_docs; help blocks are never edited by hand.

nodes.label: Retention by Data Class
nodes.rationale: Retention applies per data class rather than by blanket table purge so legal/contractual holds can override ordinary expiry without destroying audit or billing evidence.

nodes.label: Append-Only Audit Ledger
nodes.rationale: The ordinary application role cannot update or delete audit rows; PostgreSQL enforces this with revoked privileges and a mutation-rejecting trigger, and the ORM fails before flush.

nodes.label: Privileged Retention Workflow
nodes.rationale: Only a separate human-authorized workflow may de-identify allowed fields or crypto-shred keys, and it must append a tombstone describing its authority; it never makes retained audit identity look like an active user.

nodes.label: Domain-Derived Temporal Workflow IDs
nodes.rationale: Workflow IDs derive from domain IDs with matching idempotency keys and bounded retry; only opaque IDs, never secrets, pass through workflow history.

nodes.label: Configuration Precedence Chain
nodes.rationale: Defaults < config.json < LOOPGUARD_* env vars < CLI overrides; unknown fields fail validation instead of being silently accepted.

nodes.label: Owner-Only LOOPGUARD_HOME State Directory
nodes.rationale: Local state defaults to ~/.loopguard; on POSIX the directory must be mode 0700 and the database, socket, and PID file must be owner-only.

nodes.label: LGAPI-MANAGED-RULE-WEAKENED Guard
nodes.rationale: A preference update that would remove or lower a tenant-managed safety rule is rejected with 422; clients must preserve at least the managed severity.

nodes.label: OIDC Bearer Authentication and Permission Tags
nodes.rationale: Browser code calls the same-origin BFF and never receives the bearer token; cross-tenant identifiers are indistinguishable from absent ones and return 404.
nodes.norm_label: oidc bearer authentication and permission tags

nodes.label: Repository-Bound Signed Hook Intake
nodes.rationale: Machine hooks authenticate a bounded raw body with a scoped repository-bound HMAC credential, timestamp, and one-use nonce; source values inside JSON never establish identity.

nodes.label: Device-Signed Action Challenge Flow
nodes.rationale: The server supplies canonical bytes, a registered device signs those exact bytes, and the server verifies device/user/action binding before countersigning; stale state, replay, or invalid signature fails closed.

nodes.label: One-Use Origin-Bound Stream Tickets
nodes.rationale: Browser streams use one-use origin-bound tickets that expire within 30 seconds so access tokens never appear in URLs.

nodes.label: Idempotency Keys and Action Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Action creation never retries silently; HTTP 202 is acceptance not execution success, and ambiguous outcomes are reconciled by fetching the action by ID.

nodes.label: Unified Local Error Contract
nodes.rationale: Every CLI, daemon, and API adapter error carries the same fields (code, cause, suggested_commands, doc_url, request_id, retryable) with the fix printed first and no internal tracebacks by default.

nodes.label: Independent Version Domains
nodes.rationale: Product packages use SemVer while durable contracts (API, event schema, canonicalization, SQLite schema, Alembic revision, workflow schema) version independently so a package release never silently reinterprets stored data.

nodes.label: Action Canonicalization Versioning
nodes.rationale: Any byte-level change to canonical action bytes requires a new version; old challenges retain old bytes until expiry.

nodes.label: Forward-Only Backup-First Migrations
nodes.rationale: migrate apply creates and verifies an encrypted owner-only backup before forward migration; a newer or damaged schema is refused rather than downgraded or reinterpreted.

nodes.label: Signed Release Manifest Verification
nodes.rationale: update check verifies channel, version, minimum schema, HTTPS URL, SHA-256 digest, and Ed25519 signature but never downloads or executes the artifact.

nodes.label: Tenant Isolation Controls
nodes.rationale: Tenant is included in every lookup and DB transaction; existence is concealed with 404 (TM-01, TM-09).

nodes.label: Dual-Identity Signed Action Binding
nodes.rationale: Acceptance binds tenant, requesting user, device, key, nonce, expiry, canonical bytes and expected state so a stolen bearer cannot execute an action reviewed by another user/device (TM-02).

nodes.label: Repair Sandbox Isolation
nodes.rationale: Isolated worker with command/path allowlists, no host mounts/socket/token, denied network, and resource/time budgets keeps malicious repair code away from credentials and cloud metadata (TM-05).

nodes.label: Release Supply-Chain Controls
nodes.rationale: Untrusted CI jobs lack registry/cloud credentials; the release evidence verifier requires checksum, SBOM, provenance, and signature (TM-10).

nodes.label: Availability Never Outranks Safety
nodes.rationale: Unknown ownership, stale state, or ambiguous action delivery fails closed; local guarding must survive cloud, identity, or billing unavailability.

nodes.label: Trust Boundary Enforcement Table
nodes.rationale: Every transition (hook to daemon, daemon to cloud, client to API, review to execution, sandbox to GitHub, app to database, CI to release, operator to tenant) is an authenticated validated boundary with named automated evidence.

nodes.label: Independent Identity Domains
nodes.rationale: Tenant, user, device, host, repository, session, event, action, repair, and artifact identifiers are independent domains; a valid identifier in one never authorizes another, and unpredictability is not authorization.

nodes.label: Host Execution Adapter
nodes.rationale: The prompt detects whether the host is Codex or Claude Code and substitutes equivalent native tools; a missing named skill or MCP server is never a blocker.

nodes.label: Resumable Progress Protocol
nodes.rationale: A progress file with immutable task IDs, expected commit subjects, and next exact action lets any resumed session verify state and continue without redoing completed tasks.

nodes.label: 13-Tranche Execution Order
nodes.rationale: 88 numbered tasks across 11 plans execute in dependency-ordered tranches; an undeclared later API is a dependency defect fixed in the owning plan first, never implemented early for convenience.

nodes.label: LoopGuard Cloud Mobile App + Server Plan
nodes.norm_label: loopguard cloud mobile app + server plan

nodes.label: on_observe/on_pause Engine Hooks
nodes.rationale: Two tiny hooks let a non-terminal front-end stream a run and control a loop trip without adding terminal code to the core engine.

nodes.label: Run WebSocket Message Protocol
nodes.rationale: Message type strings (event, decision_required, status, done, error) and intervene actions are the exact backend-to-app contract shared by schemas.py, runs.py, app.py, runReducer.ts and client.ts.

nodes.label: Intervention Action Mapping
nodes.rationale: terminate/approve/inject/continue_once map onto LoopDecision fields so a human intervention resumes or stops a paused guarded run.

nodes.label: Two-Layer Loop Detection Architecture
nodes.rationale: Layer 1 deterministic detectors are free and offline; Layer 2 LLM judging is optional and only reasons about already-flagged loops, keeping token cost at zero in the common path.

nodes.label: Static Token-Weighted Pricing Table
nodes.rationale: No hardcoded cost or token numbers anywhere outside pricing.py's static table; unknown models report zero with a warning.

nodes.label: Phone UI Redesign Plan
nodes.rationale: Rebuilds the Expo app as a sober native-feeling operational console without changing application behavior; forbids raw colours, emoji icons, glass surfaces, and decorative stripes.

nodes.label: Workbench/Midnight Design System
nodes.rationale: Design recorded in cloud-app/design.md with portable OKLCH tokens in cloud-app/tokens.css; Space Grotesk, IBM Plex Sans, and IBM Plex Mono as the three approved font roles.

nodes.label: AdapterCapabilities Contract
nodes.rationale: Every adapter declares an explicit capability set and returns typed capability errors so unsupported controls are never silently no-oped or invented.

nodes.label: Fail-Open 100ms Hook Client
nodes.rationale: Observation hooks exit 0 when the daemon is down so agent sessions never break; a typed blocking response is returned only under an explicitly configured fail-closed policy. Socket resolution comes from trusted local configuration, never hook input.

nodes.label: Hook-to-ControlEvent Normalization
nodes.rationale: Vendor hook names map to EventKind values (Stop is turn completion, not session termination); hook payload fields are untrusted observations and repo identity resolves from the canonical Git root.

nodes.label: Gated RepairState Machine
nodes.rationale: Reproduction must precede evaluation and a verified candidate must precede publication; state transitions are methods, not arbitrary field assignment.

nodes.label: FailureEvent Normalization
nodes.rationale: Failure adapters normalize Airflow, OpenLineage, GitHub Actions, and signed webhook inputs into one FailureEvent shape with cross-source fingerprinting.

nodes.label: Draft-PR-Only Publication
nodes.rationale: The durable repair workflow permits only draft pull-request publication of the smallest verified repair; it never merges or deploys.

nodes.label: Warm Browser Broker
nodes.rationale: A version-pinned Node broker keeps browser server processes warm to cut startup latency; a standalone page.run API does not count as Playwright-test acceleration.

nodes.label: Bounded Framed Broker Protocol
nodes.rationale: Zod-validated discriminated commands over bounded length-prefixed frames; unknown fields/versions rejected, context capability IDs unguessable and session-bound, no cookies or page HTML in logs.

nodes.label: Per-Session BrowserContext Isolation
nodes.rationale: The browser process is reused but context storage never is; each worker/session gets a fresh isolated BrowserContext and closing a session destroys every page and context.

nodes.label: Tenant-Scoped Durable Event Ingest
nodes.rationale: The local daemon opens an authenticated outbound WebSocket and uploads redacted event batches; FastAPI persists tenant-scoped records in PostgreSQL before acknowledging, so acceptance is never claimed ahead of durability. Duplicate events are idempotent.

nodes.label: Change Journal
nodes.rationale: Derives repository state from control events plus filesystem reconciliation; hook and filesystem provenance merge only when repository, worktree, path, hashes, and the reconciliation window identify the same physical transition, preserving history for repeats.

nodes.label: Advisory File/Symbol Leases
nodes.rationale: Concurrent agents acquire advisory leases and are warned before their work overlaps rather than being blocked by mandatory locks.

nodes.label: Structured Agent Handoff
nodes.rationale: Codex-to-Claude and Claude-to-Codex handoff transfers decisions, changes, tests, risks, and a cursor as bounded digests instead of replaying full transcripts or hidden chain-of-thought.

nodes.label: ControlEvent Canonical Envelope
nodes.rationale: A versioned canonical event stream under loopguard.control; adapters emit ControlEvent objects that are validated and persisted before evaluation, with selected payloads projecting into the legacy LoopEvent.

nodes.label: Canonical Cursor Sequence Domains
nodes.rationale: local_log_seq, repo_seq, session_seq, cloud_ingest_seq, and client_stream_seq encode distinct domains and are never substituted for one another, so one stream cannot create a false gap in another.

nodes.label: DaemonServices Composition Root
nodes.rationale: The composition root owns per-session guards and registered subsystem handlers so event ingestion cannot silently stop at storage; persistence without dispatch is not a completed foundation.

nodes.label: PolicyDecision/ActionRequest Contract
nodes.rationale: ActionRequest carries expected_state_version, expected_state_hash, nonce, and expires_at bound to the originating PolicyDecision so remote actions execute only against the exact reviewed state.

nodes.label: iOS and Web Control Surfaces Plan
nodes.norm_label: ios and web control surfaces plan

nodes.label: Capability-Derived Navigation
nodes.rationale: Navigation derives from GET /v1/capabilities rather than hard-coded promises; Repairs is absent, not disabled-looking, until Auto-Heal registers a fresh ready capability, and every visible destination has a route-inventory test.

nodes.label: Locked Product-Design Contract
nodes.rationale: Production clients reuse the Expo prototype's operational-workbench vocabulary without copying its implementation; web tokens derive from cloud-app/tokens.css, iOS uses system typography with Liquid Glass only for iOS 26 navigation.

nodes.label: Productization Master Plan
nodes.rationale: Master coordinator of 11 executable subsystem plans; ships local value first, then managed execution, hosted surfaces, repair workflows, and enterprise hardening. Supersedes the three June prototype plans.

nodes.label: LoopEvent-LoopGuard-LoopDecision Circuit Breaker
nodes.rationale: The existing deterministic loop detector is preserved as a stable inner library while independently deployable control-plane subsystems are built around a versioned event contract.

nodes.label: Model Routing and Cost Control Plan
nodes.norm_label: model routing and cost control plan

nodes.label: Signed Provider-Neutral Model Catalog
nodes.rationale: No permanent latest model is embedded; entries come from signed configuration with source, key ID, and expiry, unknown prices stay None and never drive cost-optimized selection, and Decimal is used from parse through accounting.

nodes.label: Zero-Token TaskProfile Extractor
nodes.rationale: A deterministic feature extractor classifies task type, risk, and required capabilities without any model call, so routing itself never spends tokens.

nodes.label: Shadow Routing
nodes.rationale: Routing decisions are recorded in shadow mode before automatic routing is enabled, proving cost reduction without reducing verified success.

nodes.label: Layered Preference Sources
nodes.rationale: Sources compile into ordered hard rules, repository conventions, explicit user preferences, and learned soft preferences; deterministic evaluators run before any bounded visual critic.

nodes.label: Learned Preferences Stay Soft
nodes.rationale: Subjective model-learned preferences may never become blocking policy; only explicit hard rules block automatically, enforced by a model validator that rejects learned+block rules.

nodes.label: Production Security and Operations Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: production security and operations implementation plan

nodes.label: Production Threat Model
nodes.rationale: Critical abuse paths are encoded as failing tests first; every critical/high abuse path must link to a test, owner, and mitigation, and controls missing from earlier owning plans are moved back into those plans.

nodes.label: Signed Release Provenance
nodes.rationale: Every release artifact requires checksum, SBOM, provenance attestation, and Sigstore signature; provider credentials are never available to jobs that execute untrusted repository code, and ordinary PRs build/verify but never publish.

nodes.label: Metering, Billing Reconciliation, and Quota Safety
nodes.rationale: Billing failure never disables local guarding or deletes evidence; usage is an append-only idempotent ledger that invoices must reconcile to, and quota exhaustion never terminates local protection.
nodes.norm_label: metering, billing reconciliation, and quota safety

nodes.label: Repair Worker Sandbox Isolation
nodes.rationale: Repair workers execute untrusted repository code, so they get a dedicated node pool/namespace/service account, deny-all NetworkPolicy, no cloud metadata or service-account token, no hostPath or container socket, and a gVisor RuntimeClass or isolated microVM backend.

nodes.label: ProofContract
nodes.rationale: A contract requires at least one acceptance criterion and one check; acceptance text auto-derived from a raw prompt stays a draft until a trusted rule or actor confirms it.

nodes.label: Bounded CommandRunner
nodes.rationale: Never shell=True, empty environment plus allowlist, network denied by default, resource and output limits, and an honest unsandboxed label when the platform cannot provide a real isolation boundary.

nodes.label: BaselineService
nodes.rationale: Capturing pre-existing failures before the first mutation is what allows new failures to be distinguished from old ones instead of blaming the agent for inherited breakage.

nodes.label: ImpactAnalyzer
nodes.rationale: Every selected test must carry an explanation edge; a missing or stale index falls back to the conservative trusted full suite and never guesses a smaller one.

nodes.label: VerificationVerdict
nodes.rationale: Set-based comparison of baseline versus current failure IDs deterministically separates regression from verified_with_preexisting_failures; any required timeout, skip, or parser error prevents verified.

nodes.label: Immutable VerificationService and Evidence Store
nodes.rationale: Completed verifications are immutable; evidence is content-addressed, encrypted, and bound by a signed manifest because mutable paths and database hashes without stored bytes are not evidence.

nodes.label: Proof Ownership Rule
nodes.rationale: A result is called verified only when task intake, proof contract, clean pre-mutation snapshot, and required baseline were recorded before the first mutating tool; unproven ordering yields inconclusive or checks-passed-unbaselined, never verified.

nodes.label: LoopGuard Cloud Mobile Monitoring and Intervention App Design
nodes.norm_label: loopguard cloud mobile monitoring and intervention app design

nodes.label: Engine Hooks on_observe and on_pause
nodes.rationale: These two callbacks are the only core changes so the engine stays UI-free; terminal behavior is unchanged when the hooks are absent, letting a non-terminal front-end observe and control runs.

nodes.label: LoopGuard FastAPI Server Backend
nodes.rationale: A React Native app cannot run the Python engine in-process, so the engine runs behind a local FastAPI server that is cloud-shaped in every way except the host; built and tested like real software so it survives judge scrutiny.

nodes.label: LoopGuard v2 From Showcase to Real Product Design
nodes.norm_label: loopguard v2 from showcase to real product design

nodes.label: Layer 1 Deterministic Detectors
nodes.rationale: Kept always-on because they are deterministic, free, and offline; they are the cheap tripwire that flags suspected loops and the only requirement for offline mode.

nodes.label: Layer 2 LLM Judge
nodes.rationale: The judge calls the provider directly, never through guard.observe(), so judging cannot trip the guard on itself; on provider failure it falls back to Layer 1's decision (fail-safe, never silently fail-open), and its own token cost is tracked as a judge meta-cost.

nodes.label: LLMProvider Protocol
nodes.rationale: A thin protocol decouples the judge and live agent from any specific vendor; LiteLLMProvider gives one code path to every provider including local models, with a direct CerebrasProvider for minimal-deps runs.

nodes.label: Real Cost Pricing Model
nodes.rationale: Cost comes from real token usage and known prices; an unknown model yields 0.0 plus a one-time warning rather than an invented number, and offline runs are honestly $0.00.

nodes.label: Action Modes pause/flag/auto
nodes.rationale: Decision and response are deliberately decoupled: what to do about a confirmed loop is a policy, and UI/transport stays out of the core so the same engine can be wrapped by dashboards and the future cloud app.

nodes.label: Workbench Midnight Design System
nodes.rationale: Decoration is removed in favor of information density for operators supervising agent runs; Space Grotesk display, IBM Plex Sans body, IBM Plex Mono telemetry, one cobalt accent, and semantic status colors that always pair with text or an icon so status is never color alone.

nodes.label: ControlEvent Envelope
nodes.rationale: Introduced so the product layer does not turn LoopEvent into a universal event object; adapters project relevant ControlEvent payloads into existing LoopEvents, keeping the loop detector small while other subsystems evolve independently.

nodes.label: loopguardd Local Daemon
nodes.rationale: The trusted local coordinator: Unix socket/named pipe, SQLite WAL, redaction before persistence or relay, outbound-only cloud connection, and continued useful local operation when the cloud is unavailable.

nodes.label: AgentAdapter Protocol
nodes.rationale: Capabilities are negotiated per surface; unsupported operations return a typed CapabilityUnavailable result rather than silently doing nothing, and no adapter substitutes one lifecycle operation for another.

nodes.label: Signed ActionRequest Flow
nodes.rationale: The phone never connects directly to the daemon; a device-signed expiring request countersigned by a rotating cloud key lets the daemon verify user, device, tenant, target, nonce, expiry, capability, and state version before acting, and API 202 acceptance is never displayed as execution success.

nodes.label: Change Journal
nodes.rationale: Records file hashes, patches, symbols, actor, and a monotonic repository cursor so concurrent agents coordinate through compact verified context instead of copied transcripts or hidden reasoning.

nodes.label: Regression Verification Subsystem
nodes.rationale: Proof Core ships before the full context index because trusted discovery, pre-mutation baseline, conservative fallback, deterministic verdict, and immutable evidence are independently useful; a missing or stale index can never weaken the final gate.

nodes.label: Deterministic Model and Effort Router
nodes.rationale: The initial router is deterministic policy, not an LLM: it never selects a model unavailable on the current surface, records considered candidates and reasons, and online learning is explicitly excluded from the first release.

nodes.label: Layered Preference Engine
nodes.rationale: Safety rules, repository conventions, explicit user preferences, then learned soft preferences; deterministic rules run first and a subjective violation stays a warning unless the user promotes it to blocking.

nodes.label: Browser Broker
nodes.rationale: Warm Playwright processes with a fresh isolated BrowserContext per run; iteration uses impacted smoke tests while merge gates stay comprehensive, and speed claims compare against native Playwright worker reuse.

nodes.label: Auto-Healing Pipelines
nodes.rationale: Repairs reproduce failures in isolated sandboxes at immutable revisions, generate independent candidates, and open evidence-rich draft PRs; workers get no production write credentials and the first release never deploys or merges a repair automatically.

nodes.label: Independent Cursor Domains
nodes.rationale: local_log_seq, repo_seq, session_seq, cloud_ingest_seq, and client_stream_seq are deliberately non-interchangeable orders; every field and API uses its full domain name to prevent cursor confusion across host, repository, session, ingest, and delivery.

nodes.label: Tutorial: Prove Your First Protected Session
nodes.norm_label: tutorial: prove your first protected session

nodes.label: loopguard quickstart Command
nodes.rationale: Exercises the real framed daemon, redaction, encrypted event store, projection, detector, durable acknowledgement, and cleanup with zero provider keys and zero telemetry, so the first-run proof is the real decision path rather than a staged success message.

nodes.label: loopguard doctor Command
nodes.rationale: Reports unsupported or unsafe capabilities instead of enabling them optimistically, and never prints keys or raw tracebacks.

nodes.label: Staged Auto-Heal Rollout Modes
nodes.rationale: Promotion through observe, reproduce, generate, and publish-draft is an explicit policy-administrator update gated on measured thresholds, never an automatic response to a metric; one incident blocks promotion and demotion can happen immediately.

nodes.label: BrowserBenchmarkPolicy
nodes.rationale: Browser reuse stays disabled per repository until its own pinned benchmark shows at least a 20% improvement at both p50 and p95 with 30 post-warm-up samples, 30 full-gate correctness observations, and no isolation, reporter, trace, or selection-escape regression; otherwise the decision stays disabled with a machine-readable reason.

nodes.label: Cerebras Integration (Optional)
nodes.rationale: Cerebras is an optional live-LLM demo provider only; the demo exits gracefully without an API key so core tests and local demos never depend on it, keeping the guard local and provider-independent.

nodes.label: Semantic Loop Detection
nodes.rationale: Targets the failure mode where an agent repeatedly calls the same tool with slightly different arguments (similarity 0.91 across the last 3 tool calls) — nothing crashes, but tokens burn every step; this silent cost is why the guard exists.

nodes.label: Guard Intervention Menu
nodes.rationale: When the guard trips, the human chooses terminate, continue once, allowlist, or inject correction; injection lets the operator redirect the agent (e.g. from package.json to pyproject.toml) and recover the session instead of killing it.

nodes.label: No-Guard Demo Mode
nodes.rationale: Deliberately shows ten repeated read_file(...package.json...) attempts with rising cost to demonstrate the baseline pain before the guarded run.

nodes.label: Protected Session Setup (loopguard setup)
nodes.rationale: Setup selects one compatible integration source per agent (plugin when supported in scope, otherwise one fallback), preserves existing settings and unrelated hooks, and is idempotent (repeated setup is a no-op); project scope uses repository-owned fallback hooks when a global plugin cannot honor the boundary.

nodes.label: Explicit Vendor Trust Review
nodes.rationale: LoopGuard never clicks, writes, or bypasses a vendor trust decision; the final setup status before trust is deliberately 'attention_required' so the user must review the exact hook definition and checksum in the vendor UI and grant trust themselves, then verify with loopguard integrations verify.

nodes.label: Attention States
nodes.rationale: Named states (trust_required, hooks_not_discovered, incomplete, probe_failed, daemon unreachable, cloud conditional, setup failed) each map to a concrete next action, and none of them are treated as full protection — honesty over reassurance.

nodes.label: LoopGuard User Daemon Service
nodes.rationale: Owner-only local daemon installed per platform: macOS user LaunchAgent, Linux user systemd unit, Windows current-user scheduled task; Windows automatic startup stays experimental until named-pipe transport and ACL behavior pass the real Windows compatibility matrix.

nodes.label: protected_attached Coverage State
nodes.rationale: The coverage list (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, ...) is exact for the verified vendor/version rather than a generic 'fully protected' claim; controls outside the list remain unavailable or conditional.

nodes.label: DX Report Privacy Model
nodes.rationale: The DX report stores only fixed step names, durations, timestamps, and outcome codes; it excludes paths, repository names, prompts, credentials, and identifiers, and upload is off by default; the feedback command sends nothing automatically.

nodes.label: Uninstall vs Data Purge Separation
nodes.rationale: Uninstall removes the integration but keeps local history; permanent deletion requires a separate 'loopguard data purge --confirm', and purge refuses to orphan an installed service so data cannot be destroyed while a service still writes to it.

nodes.label: Capability State Model
nodes.rationale: Four states (supported, conditional, experimental, unavailable) derived from runtime evidence: a configured file is not proof an agent loaded or trusted it, and automation must branch on explicit capability states, never on the presence of a settings file alone.

nodes.label: Agent Capability Matrix
nodes.rationale: Per-surface matrix (Codex/Claude Code, attached/managed/cloud) over eight controls (observe, block tool, request approval, start managed, inject, interrupt, select model, select effort); cloud observation stays conditional until a real signed-delivery smoke records an event, and cloud control capabilities are never inferred from local hook configuration.

nodes.label: loopguard doctor Diagnostics
nodes.rationale: The authoritative capability report on the current machine; each surface reports vendor version, active integration source, pinned plugin checksum, hook locations, observable trust status, exact event coverage, and daemon/managed-bridge health.

nodes.label: Windows Automatic Startup (Experimental)
nodes.rationale: The current-user scheduled task (definition, SID binding, quoting, restart policy, upgrade, uninstall) is fully implemented, but LoopGuard refuses to report it as supported until named-pipe transport and current-user ACL behavior pass on a real Windows CI runner — implementation alone does not earn the supported label.

nodes.label: Safe Maintenance Boundaries
nodes.rationale: doctor --fix-safe repairs only owner-only permissions for real LoopGuard files and never changes vendor trust, credentials, policy, or unrelated configuration; uninstall removes only exact LoopGuard-owned definitions and never treats similar-looking third-party hooks or services as its own.

nodes.label: Diagnostics Bundle Redaction
nodes.rationale: Sharing diagnostics is a two-step preview-then-confirm flow (--bundle, then --confirm-bundle); the archive excludes credentials, prompts, repository names, session identifiers, and absolute hook paths, and no upload ever occurs.

nodes.label: acme-cli Demo Project (npm-manifest)
nodes.rationale: A Python CLI whose metadata lives in pyproject.toml — the trap scenario where an agent loops hunting for a nonexistent npm package.json manifest.

nodes.label: acme-data Sandbox Project
nodes.rationale: Sample repo for ad-hoc agent tasks containing real readable files: pyproject.toml, config.json, data/customers.csv, and src/pipeline.py (the data pipeline).

nodes.label: LoopGuard Verified Pipeline Repair PR
nodes.rationale: Golden fixture for the heal flow's PR body: reproduction, candidate matrix, root cause, data contract delta, verification evidence, and rollback are all mandatory sections.

nodes.label: Failure Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: A hash identity for the original failure plus pipeline/step, exact command argument array, and a reproduction artifact — repair only counts if the fingerprinted failure reproduced before the patch and the same replay passed after it.

nodes.label: Repair Candidate Matrix
nodes.rationale: Candidates are scored across replay, regression, security, contract compatibility, and diff size; the winner is chosen by least verified risk, not by biggest fix.

nodes.label: normalize_ingestion_boundary Strategy
nodes.rationale: A boundary repair strategy: normalize data at the ingestion boundary rather than patching downstream logic, chosen because the boundary fix carries the least verified risk.

nodes.label: Repair Verification Evidence
nodes.rationale: Evidence includes the evaluation artifact, verification duration, risk penalty, and the sha256 of the winning patch — the repair is auditable, not just asserted.

nodes.label: Repair Rollback Plan
nodes.rationale: Every repair is a single commit so rollback is trivially 'revert the single repair commit and rerun the original pipeline'.

nodes.label: LoopGuard Control API
nodes.rationale: Hosted control plane built health/error-contract boundary first, with database, auth, relay, streaming, action, artifact, workflow, and client endpoints landing in later tasks; production settings deliberately have no usable secret defaults — KMS/signing, PostgreSQL, OIDC, storage, Temporal, browser origins, and trusted proxies must all be configured explicitly.

nodes.label: Redacted Event Ingestion
nodes.rationale: The control plane accepts only authenticated, redacted local events and exposes tenant-scoped monitoring and control APIs — redaction happens before events ever leave the local machine.
